clause: §9.3 (open destroys the slot and replies compareClosed:true) + untruthful STATE
claim: [fable51 triage: §9.19(d); engine half — set err.extra = {compareClosed:true} on the rethrow; the renderer owner handles R-E1] `open` destroys the compare slot before `openDocument(pdf)`. If that open then throws (corrupt or invalid bytes), the error reply has no compareClosed: the engine slot is gone, the renderer (renderer.ts:1765-1767 returns early) keeps compareDoc, STATE compare.open stays true, and the next compare-render fails with no-compare-document.
reproduction: probe.mjs: main hello.pdf, then compare-open paddedPdf(MAX_PDF_BYTES - hello), then `open` a 4 KiB buffer holding '%PDF-1.4 garbage'. Result: {ok:false, compareClosed:null, session.compare:null, main still hello.pdf}.
fix: When compareClosed is true, wrap openDocument + detect in try/catch and set err.extra = {compareClosed:true} before rethrowing (the dispatch catch already spreads `extra`). Renderer: the catch in openDocument calls clearCompare() when the rejection carries compareClosed.

clause: §9.7 (on success the new doc is stored, THEN the previous one is destroyed)
claim: No test proves that the previous compare doc is destroyed. Mutant M1 (delete `if (previous) closeDocument(previous.doc)` in compare-open) passes all 9 engine tests, so a leak of a whole WASM document per re-compare would go unnoticed.
reproduction: mutants.sh: M1_noDestroyPrev on a scratch copy of build/ → `# pass 9 # fail 0` (CI_NO_ELECTRON=1 node --test tests/p6-compare.test.mjs).
fix: In test (c), after the second successful compare-open, keep the old s.compare.doc and assert.throws(() => old.countPages()), or count destroys through a wrapped mupdf.Document.openDocument.

clause: §9.3 (refuse at cap + 1; the cap itself opens)
claim: [fable51 triage: nit upgraded to should — one line; §9.3 boundary] The cap boundary itself is not pinned: mutant M7 (`>` changed to `>=` in the compare-open size check) survives.
reproduction: mutants.sh M7_capOffByOne → pass 9 fail 0. probe.mjs shows the real code opens paddedPdf(MAX - hello) beside hello (ok:true, one open).
fix: Add to (c2): op(s,{op:'compare-open', pdf: paddedPdf(MAX_PDF_BYTES - helloBytes)}).ok === true.

claim: [fable51 triage: §9.19(e)] The overlay is stretched to the .compare-b grid cell, not to B's canvas, so the red pixels land away from B's real pixels. (a) Same-size pages in a wide workspace: B shows at 612 CSS px, the overlay at 818 CSS px. (b) Portrait A vs landscape B: a 792x792 overlay is squeezed to B's cell (y-scale 0.768 vs B's 0.593), so the red 'Landscape' sits about 60 px below the black one and runs past B's bottom edge.
reproduction: node .quad/shared/p6/checks/review-compare-renderer-wide.mjs (Emulation width 2200: overlay 818 vs B 612, review-out/review-compare-i-wide-overlay.png); review-compare-renderer-mouse.mjs b (box-a.pdf vs land.pdf: overlayScale [0.593,0.768] vs bScale [0.593,0.593], review-compare-e-portrait-vs-landscape.png)
fix: Use .compare-b{position:relative;width:fit-content;max-width:100%}. In paintCompare (renderer.ts:7454-7486) size the overlay to B: new ImageData(b.pixelWidth,b.pixelHeight), marking only in-B pixels; keep differing/total counted over maxW×maxH.

claim: [fable51 triage: §9.12 + §9.19(h)] If an encrypted main is opened while compare is open, runCompare nulls text/pixels but leaves the previous document's A canvas, list and summary on screen. After the password, applyUnlocked (:1981-2004) never calls refreshCompare. The page titled encrypted.pdf keeps showing box-a.pdf's canvas and the old 'Page 1 vs 1 … 0.2 %' summary, while STATE compare.text/pixels stay null until a page turn.
reproduction: review-compare-renderer-mouse.mjs run b: open box-a, compare (insert-from land.pdf), open fixtures/encrypted.pdf, then the password step → the 'after unlock' log shows text:null, pixels:null, the stale summary and an unchanged A hash; screenshots review-compare-f-encrypted-main.png and review-compare-g-after-unlock.png
fix: In runCompare's needsPassword branch, clear the three canvases, the list body and the summary. End applyUnlocked with `if (compareDoc) await refreshCompare(true);`.

clause: §9.2/§9.7 refusal reasons (read-only copy gate vs too-many)
claim: [fable51 triage: §9.19(f); also add a p2-shell source pin that both sentences exist in renderer.ts (S-3)] Every compare-text refusal renders 'this document does not permit copying'. too-many (> 2000 lines) and read-only from a locked session get the same false sentence, so the UI states an untrue reason.
reproduction: Read :7440-7444: `text.refused ? '…does not permit copying…'` with no switch on the reason. A main page with > 2000 stext lines (engine test §9.7 fixture) shows the copying sentence.
fix: Branch on text.refused: 'read-only' → the copy sentence; 'too-many' → 'too many lines to compare as text, so only pixels are compared'.

Step 4 already left pageB at 2, and step 5 pins neither an error nor any change, so a build that ignores or refuses pageB 9 (showError, no state change) still passes it.

claim: No drive step, test or shot case covers the #compare-page-b change handler (renderer.ts:9529) or the PageUp/PageDown/Escape keydown handler (renderer.ts:9519). The drive's pageB calls setComparePageB directly, so a 0/1-based slip in the input handler, or a dead Escape, passes every check.

fix: In shot-compare.mjs, before the close click: CDP focus #compare-page-b, Input.insertText "3" then Tab, and expect STATE compare.pageB 2. Then send a CDP Input.dispatchKeyEvent Escape with #compare-view focused and expect compare.open false and #reader shown. Keep the #compare-close click on a reopen, or accept Escape as the close proof.

claim: [fable51 triage: merged into R3 (renderer owner); the renderer fixer adds a p2-shell source pin for both reason sentences] Every compare-text refusal (too-many at >2000 lines, no-document, read-only from a locked main) produces the summary and announcement 'this document does not permit copying'. That is untruthful for too-many. No test reaches the renderer's refused branch.
reproduction: Read runCompare: the summary branches only on text.refused being truthy, not on its value. Neither p6-compare's drive half nor compare.jsonl produces text.refused (grep 'refused' shows only engine-half assertions).
fix: Word the summary by reason (read-only → copying not permitted; too-many → 'more than 2000 lines on a page, only pixels are compared'). Pin one refused case, for example a unit on the summary helper or a drive step once a no-copy fixture exists.

clause: §9.10 / brief: exit 1 naming the chord if compare.open stays false
claim: [fable51 triage: nit upgraded to should — the chord must be named on failure] If ⌥⌘K does not open compare, the run fails with the generic 'FAIL timeout: null' and does not name the chord.
reproduction: Read the code: wait() throws `timeout: ${q(last)}`, and the catch prints FAIL plus the stack.
fix: Wrap the wait: .catch(() => { throw new Error('⌥⌘K (key code 40 using {option down, command down}) did not open compare: compare.open false'); }).

clause: brief: hit-test with elementFromPoint and log a fallback like shot-bates.mjs; wait on repaints, not sleeps
claim: [fable51 triage: nit upgraded to should — the Bates lesson: hit-test with elementFromPoint, log a fallback, wait on #status repaints] The CDP clicks on #compare-show-diff and #compare-close are made without an elementFromPoint hit-test or a logged fallback, and the script uses fixed sleep(800)/sleep(600) instead of waiting on #status.

claim: [fable51 triage: companion to E-R1] When openDocument's request rejects and the rejection carries compareClosed:true (the engine fixer sets err.extra = {compareClosed:true} on the pair-cap path), the renderer must clearCompare() (STATE compare.open false, view closed, #reader shown) and announce 'Compare closed: the two files together exceed the size limit'.
